summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell activation syndrome was admitted for chest pain and dyspnea consistent with a mast cell flare. She presented after worsening pain at her gastroenterologist’s office and reported a recent fall without loss of consciousness. Initial evaluation ruled out acute cardiac or pulmonary pathology via EKG and chest X-ray. She was treated with IV benadryl, Ativan, and oral methadone and Dilaudid for pain and anxiety. Her home regimen for mast cell disease was continued, including cromolyn, antihistamines, and midodrine for syncope prevention. Symptoms improved, and she was discharged the following morning. Medication adjustments included reduced ranitidine and doxepin, a switch to 24-hour Adderall formulation, and replacement of cefuroxime with nitrofurantoin for UTI prophylaxis. Follow-up was emphasized with her new allergist.
